patch_description:
The current approach uses six sequential simulated-annealing restarts of 36,000 proposals, with an initial step of 0.112, lower-tail blend weight 0.085, temperature 0.0025, and a 10-scale bottleneck polish beginning at 0.018. Its main limitation is that most proposals modify only one point and are evaluated serially, making basin exploration relatively narrow.

This version replaces the long sequential annealing schedule with a vectorized population search. It uses 104 concurrent layouts, 980 generations, three complementary proposal types per generation (correlated local perturbation, differential-evolution transport, and bottleneck-targeted moves), periodic diversity injection, and a lower-tail surrogate that decays from 0.070 to zero. The final stage is strict maximin-only active-set polishing with coordinated one- and two-point proposals. All layouts remain inside a unit square with fixed corners, so the raw minimum triangle area remains exactly the hull-normalized objective.
